sub_graphs.title: EIP-2681: Transaction Nonce Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation rules for transaction nonces at the protocol level

nodes.label: Transaction Received
nodes.description: A new transaction has been received for validation

nodes.label: Extract Transaction Nonce
nodes.description: Read the nonce value from the transaction payload

nodes.label: Nonce Value Extracted
nodes.description: Transaction nonce has been parsed and is available for validation

nodes.label: Check Nonce Against Limit
nodes.description: Compare transaction nonce against maximum value 2^64-1

nodes.label: Nonce Within Valid Range
nodes.description: Transaction nonce is less than 2^64-1

nodes.label: Nonce Exceeds Maximum
nodes.description: Transaction nonce is >= 2^64-1, transaction is invalid

nodes.label: Reject Transaction
nodes.description: Mark transaction as invalid and reject from processing

nodes.label: Transaction Invalid
nodes.description: Transaction rejected due to nonce limit violation

nodes.label: Transaction Nonce Valid
nodes.description: Transaction passes nonce limit check, may proceed to other validations

external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
external_entities.description: User or application submitting a transaction to the network

sub_graphs.title: EIP-2681: Account Nonce State Transitions
sub_graphs.description: Models how account nonces change and the constraints enforced during state transitions

nodes.label: Current Account Nonce
nodes.description: The current nonce value stored in the account state

nodes.label: Execute Transaction
nodes.description: Execute a transaction that will increment the sender's nonce

nodes.label: Increment Account Nonce
nodes.description: Add 1 to the account's nonce value

nodes.label: Nonce Incremented
nodes.description: Account nonce has been successfully incremented

nodes.label: Nonce At Maximum Value
nodes.description: Account nonce equals 2^64-1, no further transactions possible

nodes.label: Account Effectively Locked
nodes.description: Account cannot submit any more transactions due to nonce limit

external_entities.name: Validated Transaction
external_entities.description: Transaction that has passed all validation checks

sub_graphs.title: EIP-2681: CREATE/CREATE2 Nonce Overflow Handling
sub_graphs.description: Models the special error handling when contract creation hits nonce limits

nodes.label: Contract Creation Initiated
nodes.description: CREATE or CREATE2 opcode execution has been initiated

nodes.label: Check Sender Nonce
nodes.description: Check the nonce of the account performing the create operation

nodes.label: Nonce Below Maximum
nodes.description: Creator account nonce is less than 2^64-1

nodes.label: Nonce At Maximum For Create
nodes.description: Creator account nonce equals 2^64-1

nodes.label: Execute Initcode
nodes.description: Execute the contract initialization code and deploy contract

nodes.label: Return Zero Without Initcode
nodes.description: Return 0 on the stack without executing initcode or deducting initcode gas

nodes.label: Contract Successfully Created
nodes.description: New contract deployed, address returned on stack

nodes.label: Create Failed Due To Nonce
nodes.description: Contract creation failed, zero returned on stack

external_entities.name: EVM Execution Context
external_entities.description: Smart contract execution that triggers CREATE/CREATE2

ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly state whether the nonce limit applies from genesis or only after the EIP activation block.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: The specification states 'retroactively from genesis', so assume the limit has always applied and no historical blocks violate this constraint.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'without deducting gas for the initcode execution' is unclear about whether other CREATE-related gas costs are still deducted.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume only initcode execution gas is not deducted; other gas costs (base cost, memory expansion) may still apply.

implicit_assumptions.description: No existing account on any Ethereum network has a nonce approaching 2^64-1.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Existing high-nonce accounts could become immediately locked, causing loss of funds.

implicit_assumptions.description: Reaching nonce 2^64-1 is practically impossible under normal operation given the transaction throughput limits.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If throughput dramatically increases, accounts could become locked, requiring protocol changes.

implicit_assumptions.description: Applications do not rely on CREATE/CREATE2 succeeding without checking the return value.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Applications may assume successful contract creation when it actually failed silently.
